verdicts.reason: Confirmed in the code. item_cost (relay.py:240-241) charges items 1 and 2 two runs per pair (relay and frozen). Neither plan_of (253-261, including the T_c rule at 258 and the kept list at 262-264) nor the re-projection (410-417) adds frozen@relay. Yet cpu_rule forces frozen@relay on every category when frozen_matched_everywhere is set (341-347), and in part b (366-368). Its first level is free: kernel/run.py key_of (137-140) has no purpose field, and a None memory digests the same, so the first level is the cached frozen run. Every raised pair then costs a new run at 2*T_c. I called plan_of with the scenario's inputs (o0 at 39 s, ratio 1.26, J=64, S=2, J2=32, R=16). At H_cap 70,000: T=200 everywhere, kept [1,2], projection 57,867. Part a plus half the pairs raised spends 43,401 machine CPU-s, and the re-projection before item 2 is 72,334 > 70,000, so r_cap fires and E-R1 is left on 32 of 64 chains (endpoint need=J, so not met). If frozen@matched were counted, the primary would be 86,800 and plan_of would lower T_c (to 160 on all four categories, 69,440) and run the whole primary. At H_cap 80,000, kept is [1,2,3]; item 2 passes at 72,334 and the stage ends at 86,801, past H_cap. This deviates from D2(f) ('plan frozen@matched for every held-out category') and from 6.2(2) (matched items count 2 levels; lower T_c when the primary alone exceeds the cap). There is a second gap even without D2(f): once part a's r_cpu_rule has fixed the matched categories, the part-b raises are certain, but cost([2]) leaves them out. So the registered check 'if the item itself does not fit the stage stops' is not enforced for item 2, and the overshoot (up to about 26,000 machine CPU-s when most pairs are raised) can exceed the 15,000 reserve. make_dev_r's H (lines 144-145) lacks the flag, so D4's plan_of call (148) has the same omission.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Add the flag to item_cost: when H.get('frozen_matched_everywhere'), items 1 and 2 cost (2 + matched_levels - 1) runs per pair at r0 (relay, the frozen run, and the extra frozen@matched levels). Before item 2, for each category in part a's r_cpu_rule matched_categories, add an estimate of the part-b raises. The best estimate is part a's measured frozen@relay CPU outside the frozen run keys, scaled by (J - J//2)/(J//2); the fallback is (matched_levels - 1) x r0 per pair. In make_dev_r, put frozen_matched_everywhere=matched_all into H before calling relay.plan_of. Spell both rules out in heldout.plan_rule (make_registration_r.py:146).

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Spec 6.2(3) says 'each item is submitted as one interleaved batch', and RESEARCH_PLAN.md (around line 282) requires 'compared arms interleaved in time on the same machine'. primary() (relay.py:361-362) makes two calls, arm('relay') and then arm('frozen'), so two Cache.get calls. kernel/run.py run() maps each list over the 4-worker pool on its own, so all relay jobs of the item finish before any frozen job starts. Item 11 (385-386) does the same with o0@ref and a0@ref. The meta stage, by contrast, does interleave on- and off-policy jobs in one batch (lines 84-95). Acquired scores do not depend on batching, because the cache key has no batch or order component. But the per-category relay/frozen CPU ratio that cpu_rule compares with 1.10 (line 339), and the want values of the frozen@relay raises, come from two disjoint time windows. Drift between those windows enters the ratio directly and can move a category across the tolerance. The raise of frozen@relay after relay is necessarily separate, but the relay and frozen runs at T_c are not.
verdicts.corrected_fix: As proposed. Build one job list per item with relay and frozen jobs interleaved per (j, c, s), and do the same for o0@ref and a0@ref in item 11. Submit it with a single cache.get, split the returned rows by arm in job order (each arm's row list, and so r_stage_done's keys, stays the same), then call add() per arm.

verdicts.reason: The facts check out. make_dev_r.py:107-109 only sets dropped_arms, and relay_changes (112-118) can only hold rule and beta. The RELAY0 assertion in make_registration_r.py (34-37) therefore passes with lib_max=32 and lib_per_run=4. relay.py:402 skips items 6 and 8. relay_report.py:521-527 removes E-R5 and treats it as met for T2 (e5=True). Meanwhile _new_entries (design_r.py:311-328) keeps writing r_lib blocks, and _variant (244-247) enables the splice cells. D2(b) says 'drop the library', which names the mechanism, and both of its stated consequences hold exactly only if the library channel is off. 'The Owner's comparison 3 then coincides with frozen' requires without(M_j, r_stats) to be empty. Removing prioronly is redundant only if prioronly equals relay. Spec 2.2 also says RELAY0 is 'changed only by D2's pre-written rules', and validate admits lib_max=0 and lib_per_run=0. As implemented, a median of 1 block in development keeps an active library over 12 positions in the registered chains, removes its controls, and lets T2 claim 'beyond retained blocks' on E-R2 and E-R4 alone.
verdicts.corrected_fix: When lib_median < 2, set relay_changes['lib_per_run'] = 0 and set the same value in design_r.RELAY0 before registering (the assertion then enforces it). lib_per_run=0 is better than lib_max=0: no r_lib entry ever enters a memory, so prioronly's memory is identical to relay's and libonly's is None, the same cache keys as relay and frozen. In the same branch, drop P5's library-size check (or mark it not applicable) in make_registration_r. It would otherwise be scored a miss at size 0. Also state the dropped channel in the D2(b) decision text.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed, minor, and no crash. At sigma 0.03 and tau 0.008, D2(a) picks (48,2) (power 0.89; it picks it while tau-hat stays below about 0.009). After a futility stop, arms relay and frozen hold chains 0-23 only. Item 4's filter (relay.py:377-378) yields 192 pairs on 24 chains, against item 4's registered j < 32, s < 2. Item 7 (line 381) runs jobs on sec=range(32), s=0, which includes 32 runs at 4*T_c on chains 24-31 that have no frozen run. The report's paired() (relay_report.py:97-111) skips those runs, so L2 is computed on 24 chains, and roughly 6,000 recorded CPU-s buy nothing any registered quantity uses. One part of the finding overstates the cost side: item 7's charge in item_cost matches what it actually runs (32 chains). Only item 4 is overcharged, and that is conservative. The real defects are that neither the spec nor the registered futility text defines the chain sets of items 4 and 7 when J/2 < secondary_chains, and that the code silently shrinks item 4's pair set while spending item 7's CPU on chains that have no frozen pair.
verdicts.corrected_fix: When stop is true and J//2 < J2, run item 7 on [j for j in sec if j < J//2] (the chains that hold frozen runs). Charge items 4 and 7 on min(J2, J//2) chains in the re-projection after the futility look (plan_of, made before the look, may keep charging 32). Add to heldout.futility that items 4 and 7 then cover the J/2 chains of primary-a. Alternatively, run relay and frozen on chains J//2 to 31 before item 4, and register that instead.
